title: Harborline Customer Accounts: Working Out a Domain Retry Top-up
content:
# Working out a domain retry top-up

**Product:** Harborline Customer Accounts

## The domain and its retry

The domain concerned is the domain of the most recently recorded declined domain auto-renew attempt while that domain is still active and its expiry date is today or later; its next retry is the first of the days 14, 7 and 1 calendar days before its expiry date, the domain charter's retry days, that is today or later. Where two declined domain auto-renew attempts share that latest recorded time, the domain concerned cannot be told from the records and the customer is outside this policy. A deposit for any other purpose is the amount the holder chooses, under the base deposit rule.

## Customers the policy handles

It handles a customer who holds at most one active hosting plan with auto-renew on, which has no scheduled downgrade, and at most one active email subscription with auto-renew on, which is neither billed annually in monthly instalments nor scheduled to change product, who holds at most one active site security plan, at most one active server and at most one active certificate subscription with auto-renew on, whose server, if any, carries no add-ons, meaning no extra IPv4 addresses, no backups, no managed support and no control panel licence, and whose account's most recent tier review neither started a downgrade grace nor found a downgrade due; any other customer's top-up is the amount the holder chooses, under the base deposit rule.

## Calculation

1. Because account credit pays an auto-renew charge only when the credit balance covers the whole charge, the top-up covers the retry charge in full.
2. The retry charge is the domain's TLD renewal price times its auto-renew term years, reduced by the account tier's domain renewal discount and rounded half up to the cent, plus the ICANN fee per year times those years, which is never discounted.
3. The credit the retry needs is the retry charge together with every other counted charge, all added together, less every discount that applies.
4. The credit balance counted is the sum of all the account's credit ledger entries.
5. The top-up deposit is the credit the retry needs less the credit balance; where that is zero or less no top-up is needed and none is taken, and otherwise the top-up is at least the tier's minimum deposit and is rounded half up to the cent.
6. A top-up that would exceed the tier's maximum per transaction, or that would raise the credit balance above the tier's maximum credit balance, is refused in full and no top-up is taken.

The TLD prices are those of the domain's product on Domain Registrations; the discount and deposit figures are those of the account's tier.

## Retry day (hypothetical dates)

| Expiry date from today | Next retry |
|---|---|
| 20 days | 6 days from today (14 days before expiry) |
| 10 days | 3 days from today (7 days before expiry) |
| 4 days | 3 days from today (1 day before expiry) |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A Harborline Reseller Bronze account (domain renewal discount 3 percent, minimum deposit $100.00) has a declined auto-renewal on a domain whose TLD renewal price is $17.30 for a 1-year auto-renew term, with an ICANN fee of $0.35, and a credit balance of $4.12. Retry charge: $17.30 reduced by 3 percent, $16.781, rounded to $16.78, plus $0.35, $17.13. Less the balance: $13.01. The top-up is at least $100.00, so it is $100.00. On a Harborline Personal Account (no discount, minimum $25.00) with a balance of $0.00 and a TLD price of $33.70, the retry charge is $34.05 and the top-up is $34.05.
